highlights.title: Find in a thread
highlights.text: Press ⌘F (Edit > Find in Thread) to search the open thread's words. Matches are marked in yellow, and Return steps through them.

media.alt: A thread with a reply holding a TypeScript code block. ⌘F opens a find bar above the thread, attempt is typed in, and each match turns yellow while Return steps from 1 of 4 to 4 of 4, the picked one brighter.

highlights.title: Type # to link a thread
highlights.text: Type # in the message box, pick another thread from the list, and it goes in as a chip the agent can read.

media.alt: Typing Use the same retry as # in the message box brings up a list of threads over it. Typing upl narrows it to Make uploads resume after a crash, and Return puts that thread in the message as a chip.

highlights.title: Coloured code blocks
highlights.text: Code in replies is coloured by its language, with a bar on top naming it and a Copy button. On the Mac, iPhone and Android.

media.alt: A reply's TypeScript code block with keywords, types and numbers in different colours, a bar on top saying TypeScript with a copy button, and a pull request link under it.

highlights.title: Sounds play in the side pane
highlights.text: Open a WAV, MP3, M4A or other sound file and it plays right in the pane. Agents can put sounds in a design review too, to compare music or effects.

media.alt: A thread opens standup-note.wav in the pane beside it, which shows a rounded player bar with play, a position slider and the time, and it plays.

highlights.title: Send it later from Send
highlights.text: The arrow beside Send offers tonight at 9 pm, tomorrow at 9 am, or when your tokens reset, each opening the schedule with that time filled in.

media.alt: A message is typed, then the arrow beside Send opens a menu with Send tonight at 9 pm, Send tomorrow at 9 am, Send when tokens reset and Schedule. Picking tomorrow opens Schedule a message with the message and 26 Nov at 9:00 am filled in.

highlights.title: Pull requests open beside the thread
highlights.text: Click a GitHub pull request link and it opens in a tab beside the thread, with its checks, changed files and Review and Merge buttons. Needs the gh command line tool.

media.alt: Clicking a pull request link in a reply opens it as a tab beside the thread, with Overview, Diff and Checks, Review and Merge buttons, its branch, status, checks with Windows failed, its description and a comment box.

highlights.title: Hide the sidebar panels with ⇧⌘B
highlights.text: ⇧⌘B tucks away Runners, Connectors, Updates, Usage and Setup under the threads list, and brings the same ones back. ⇧⌘A attaches a picture.

media.alt: The threads list with the Usage and Updates panels docked under it. ⇧⌘B tucks them away so the list runs the full height, and pressing it again brings both back.

added: New keys: ⌘` opens the Terminal, ⌘B shows the threads, ⇧⌘P opens Open Anything and ⌘L jumps to the message box.
Threads say who hibernated, woke, archived or brought them back, and when, in a grey line.
Gemini's plan usage shows in the Usage panel, like Claude's and Codex's.

added.text: Share a thread by link from its menu on iPhone and Android.

added: A new Claude thread's agent starts while you write the first message, so the first reply comes a little sooner.

changed.text: An archived thread from another Mac has Delete greyed out, and its tip says which Mac to delete it on, instead of failing after you confirm.

changed: The iPhone, Android and the website put each thread under the same heading the Mac does, as the runner now decides it for all of them.
Extra Codex logins get your usual instructions, hooks, skills and settings from your main Codex login.
Messages you send while a thread is compacting go in as soon as it's done, not after the whole turn.

changed.text: Early in a week, Usage's forecast goes by last week's pace instead of guessing from a busy first hour.
A new install sets up its own Codex straight away, without a warning while it does.

changed: A Grok login that's out of credit says so and is marked out, instead of failing turns.

fixed.text: An agent's snooze until words with a number in, like a ticket name, no longer snoozes to a year like 3843.

fixed: Your phone no longer gets a notification for a thread you've archived or hibernated.
A patch panel's button opens its panel straight away on a busy runner.

fixed.text: Building the app yourself skips a revoked Apple Development certificate.

fixed: Security: a limited thread can no longer take over another runner on the same Mac, run a planted program through a check, or get owner rights when a process lookup fails; a thread's picture can't run the app out of memory; and the app's installer, box images and self-hosted backend images are checked against pinned versions.
